name: Linocut
summary: A moving linocut print: cream paper, carbon-black key plate, one misregistered pumpkin-orange spot plate and a sparing teal.
description: Everything looks carved and printed: black ink shapes with white gouge marks cut into them, black lens-shaped knife marks on bare paper, and a single orange spot colour printed slightly off-register so a sliver of paper shows on one side. There are no gradients anywhere – tone comes only from line density, stipple and hatched shadows. The mood is a folk-tale broadsheet crossed with a screen-printed gig poster.
avoidFor: colour-coded puzzle games that need many hues
very dense hordes (they merge into black)

difficulty.why: White cut lines inside black areas are fine detail work for every figure, and large hordes already blur into one black mass.

technique.resolution: Native resolution. Sprites baked at K = clamp(round(screenH/360*4)/4, 2, 5) px per world unit; ground chunks (256 units) at up to 2.5 px per unit.
technique.summary: Figures are drawn as filled ink shapes plus filled 'lens' (gouge) and 'taper' marks in paper colour or ink, the orange plate is drawn offset by (0.8, 0.55) units, then a paper halo is put behind and an ink-void pass knocks pinholes into the black.
technique.linework: No strokes of constant width: every line is a filled lens (pointed both ends, half-width 0.12-0.85 units) or a taper (blunt start, sharp tip). Outlines are thin ink strokes 0.5-0.75 units plus a heavy 'crescent' (shape minus a shrunken copy shifted to the upper left, scale 0.93-0.96) on the shadow side.
technique.shading: Two values only (ink / paper) plus flat spot colours. Shade = parallel black lenses getting wider toward the shadow side (e.g. 6 lenses widening 0.16 -> 0.44 on the pumpkin's right), lit side = white gouges carved out of black (cloak folds, crown highlights).
technique.lighting: Fixed light from the upper left. Crescents and shadow lenses sit bottom-right, carved highlights top-left. Glows are flat orange ray stars (12-18 spikes) printed on the spot plate, never gradients.
technique.texture: Paper: 512x512 fibre map (1300 curved fibres) + mottling + grain, offset -22..+14. Ink: 256x256 void noise; where it exceeds ~238 the ink lightens 70% toward paper (pinholes). Orange gets +-6% density grain.

palette.name: Paper
palette.role: Ground, halos, carved highlights (~65% of the screen)

palette.name: Ink
palette.role: Key plate: all outlines, solid masses, marks (~30%)

palette.name: Pumpkin Orange
palette.role: The one spot plate: hero head, glowing cores, eyes of lanterns, gems, XP, crits (~4%)

palette.name: Teal
palette.role: Second spot, used sparingly: ghost frost stipple, brute core ring, big gem centre (<1%)

palette.name: Ink Deep
palette.role: Hard offset shadow on cards / panels

paletteRules: Only paper, ink and flat spot colours. No gradients, no transparency effects, no soft shadows.
Orange is always printed offset by (+0.8, +0.55) world units (mirrored x with facing); teal by (-0.55, +0.45). The same offset everywhere – that is the misregistration signature.
Spot colours appear only inside holes cut in the key plate (holeSpot) or as their own plate under an ink outline.
Tone is made with line density: wider/more black lenses = darker. Never mix grey.
Teal is an accent for at most 2-3 element types.

typography.role: Titles, clock time, card keys – western woodtype display
typography.css: font: 400 34px/1.05 'Rye', Georgia, serif; letter-spacing: 2px; color: #1b1715; text-shadow: 2px 2px 0 #ea6820;

typography.role: Numbers: HP, kills, level, damage numbers, card names
typography.css: font: 400 17px 'Alfa Slab One', Georgia, serif; color: #1b1715;

typography.role: Typewriter body text and small labels
typography.css: font: 400 11px 'Special Elite', 'Courier New', monospace; letter-spacing: 3px; border-top: 2px solid #1b1715;

background.summary: Per-pixel 'ink coverage' on fibrous paper. Noise fields with signed distances define regions; each region has a carved pattern computed analytically per pixel (grass ticks, furrows, stipple, cobbles, solid ink with echo contours) separated by 1.5-unit paper gutters. Decals are knocked out of the ground with paper discs and re-carved.
layers: Meadow: grass ticks on a 9-unit hashed grid (1-3 tapered blades, length 2.2-3.55, half-width 0.46), density 0.1-0.6, plus rare 'chatter' (3-5 parallel short gouges)
Field: ploughed furrows along a warped direction field (spacing 4.4 units, half-width up to 0.66) with a carved ditch line at the edge
Forest floor: hashed stipple dots (r 0.3-0.54 on a 2.5-unit grid, density 0.14-0.66) with a 0.84-unit edge line and a gap behind it
Dark soil: solid ink, two paper echo contours 1.8 and 3.4 units inside the edge, oriented white gouge flecks deeper inside
Road: 22-unit-wide cobbles from Worley cells (size 4.4) with paper joints, hatched stone shading on the shadow side, curb line
Ink pass: pinhole voids (VOID noise) and paper fibres showing through the ink
Decals: flowers, stars, pebbles, skulls, bones, leaves, twigs, mushrooms, sprouts snapped to furrows, carved tree roots
Props (y-sorted sprites with hatched shadows): oaks, crowned trees, spruces, graves, fences, scarecrows, lantern poles, crows, haystacks
Screen: ragged ink frame strips (t = 1.1% of H) with an inner rule

characters.summary: Bold silhouettes built from filled smooth paths, tapered limbs and lens marks. Each figure mixes a paper-filled form (with black carving) and a solid-ink form (with white gouges) so it reads on both paper and dark soil. A 0.9-unit paper halo is baked behind every sprite. 4 walk frames x 2 carving variants (re-seeded jitter) per facing.
rules: Hero ~16 x 30 units: big pumpkin head (7.3 x 6.2, 22 lobed points) on a solid-black cloak; head = paper + offset orange plate + black ribs and shading lenses + heavy crescent + carved black face.
Every form has one solid area: cloak, turnip crown, brute body. Faces are carved: paper lens eyes in black, or black holes in paper.
The orange plate is used for the single most important element per character (hero head, brute core, lantern face).
Light from the upper left: crescent shadow bottom-right, white gouge highlights top-left.
Keep 0.9 units of paper halo around sprites so black figures on black soil and black hordes stay separable.
Animation is stepped: carving variants swap at 6 fps, never smooth tweening of shapes.

effects.name: Spawn: block stamped down
effects.how: For spawnT < 0.5 the sprite is drawn larger (1 + (1-k)^2 * 0.9) and 10 units higher with alpha 0.25 -> 1 as the block is lowered; on impact an ink splat is stamped on the ground and the sprite squashes (sin * 0.14).

effects.name: Death: carved shatter
effects.how: 0.16 s negative print (paper/ink inverted), then the sprite is cut into 4-5 pre-baked wedge shards whose fresh cut edges show paper; shards fly outward, rotate +-1.6 rad and fall with alpha 1 - u^2. An ink splat stays on the ground.

effects.name: Hit flash = negative print
effects.how: A baked inverted copy (paper <-> ink by luminance, spot colours turn black) is shown while flash > 0.45; the hero blinks between normal and negative at 14 Hz.

effects.name: Projectile
effects.how: Orange seed plate offset by the misregistration under a black outlined seed with a carved shine; trail = 3 black lenses behind it, scaled in over 0.12 s; rotation snapped to 45-degree steps * 0.35.

effects.name: Orbiting lantern
effects.how: Turnip lantern with an orange face hole, over a slowly rotating 14-spike orange ray star printed offset by (MX, MY).

effects.name: Particles
effects.how: Ink drops (blobs + satellites), wood chips (black or paper lenses with a carved line), radial black/orange lens bursts, halftone puffs (hex dot grid whose dots shrink to the edge, 3 frames), orange 4-point stars, orange gouge-arc rings for level up.

ui.summary: Letterpress HUD: paper panels with a noise texture, 3 px ink borders, hard 4 px ink offset shadows, small radii (2 px), stepped transitions. Bars are diagonal stripe fills (orange with ink rules for XP, ink with paper rules for HP). The clock sits in a double-ruled box with a 7 px hard shadow.

motion: Carving boil: 2 variants per frame (different jitter seeds), swapped at 6 fps.
Hero walk: 4 key poses (foot positions 3.3/-3.0, bob -0.8 on passing frames, cloak hem and scarf swing), idle 2 poses at 2.2 fps.
Small enemy: 4 frames, bob -0.75*|sin|, tilt 0.075*cos; ghost floats 2.2 units up with a bob quantised to 0.4-unit steps.
Damage numbers pop from 170% to 100% in 0.07 s and fade in the last 0.22 s.
UI transitions are stepped (steps(2) / steps(3)) like a print being swapped, never smooth.
do: Build everything from filled lenses, tapers, limbs and smooth paths – no constant-width strokes.
Give each figure one solid black mass with white carving and one paper area with black carving.
Print orange on its own plate with the same fixed offset everywhere.
Use a heavy crescent on the bottom-right and white gouges on the top-left (light from upper left).
Bake a paper halo around sprites and pinhole voids into the ink.
Use hatched (lens line) shadows under actors.
Keep regions separated by paper gutters and carved edge lines.
dont: Don't use gradients, blur, glow or alpha-blended shading.
Don't add more spot colours; orange plus a sparing teal is the limit.
Don't register colour perfectly inside outlines – the offset sliver is the look.
Don't draw uniform hairlines or vector-clean strokes.
Don't animate smoothly with tweens on shapes; swap stepped variants.
Don't put black enemies on black ground without a paper halo.
performance: All character frames (4 x 2 variants x 2 facings), negative copies and death shards, props, particles and shadows are baked at init; the expensive steps are getImageData passes (inkify, invert). Ground chunks are generators that yield every 8 rows inside a 5 ms per-frame budget: an 84x84 field grid per chunk, then per-pixel analytic patterns (grass hash cells, furrows, Worley cobbles) – Worley on roads and hashed cells elsewhere are the hot spots. Per frame is only drawImage of cached sprites.
